To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetic architecture of morphological variability differs between populations, that the relative dominance is high in the population where biotic selection is strong and the additive-genetic variability is low, and that the relative dominance appears to be low in the population where abiotic selection is strong and additive-genetic variability high.
the populations differed significantly in the genetic control of the characters.

the genetic variability in both populations is differentially determined, and that in the biotic controlled population, the genetic variability of the characters is lower than in the abiotic controlled population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic analysis of morphological variability, which is ecologically relevant, i.e. it is a part of the adaptive variability of the plant.
the genetic architecture of ecologically relevant variability in a perennial plant.
the genetic basis of morphological variability in two populations of P. lanceolata.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative dominance is higher and additive-genetic variability is lower in Me than in Wd.
the relative dominance in the Wd population was lower than in the Me population, and that additive-genetic variability was higher in the Wd than in the Me populations.
the relative dominance is high in the population where biotic selection is assumed to be strong, and that the additive-genetic variance is low in both populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic variability of the populations was not only determined by the genetic architecture but that the environment also plays a role in this respect.

the genetic analysis of the ecologically important variability in the populations of P. lanceolata is possible and that it is a promising approach to understand the genetic basis of the variability of ecologically relevant characters.
the populations were differentiated in life history, in genetic variability, in genetic architecture, and in relative contributions of genetic variance components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic basis of ecologically relevant traits can be assessed by using a combination of genetic and ecological methods.

the model of C. & W. provides a useful tool to study the contribution of the genetic variance components to the variability in a population and to study how the genetic variance components contribute to the genetic architecture of the population.
the relative importance of genetic and environmental components to variability is population dependent.
